analysis.title: Daily Points, October 27, 2026
key_insights: Markets are described as buying time ahead of an active calendar of global risks running through next week. Equities are broadly higher, sovereign bonds slightly richer except the long end in France, oil is slightly cheaper, and currencies are mixed against the dollar.
The author recommends fading headlines on Canada-US trade negotiations. Canada is talking the talks down while Trump and Hassett talk them up, which resembles the path to the August breakdown.

Bloomberg's consensus for the Bank of Canada decision (median 2.375%, between 2.25% and 2.5%) is called misleading. Removing TD's two hold entries and the 'tourist' forecasters swings the consensus to a hike to 2.5%.
Five of the six major domestic banks now call for a BoC hike on October 28. The Wall Street Journal poll last week showed 11 of 15 economists expecting +25bps, and OIS prices a hike at over 80%.
A widely expected FOMC hold is due October 28. US data on October 27 includes durable goods, Case-Shiller home prices, consumer confidence and new home sales.

Israel's election results may take days or longer because of vote counting and coalition formation. The vote is expected to be very close, and the outcome could influence the direction of the war with Iran.

The RBNZ is expected to hike on October 27 at 9pmET, and Chile's BCCh is expected to hold at 5pmET. The RBA is 15bps priced for a hike at its November 2 decision, with Governor Bullock testifying to parliament at 8:15pmET.

Anthropic's S-1 prospectus carries warnings of catastrophic and existential AI risk, including self-preserving model behavior and uninsurable losses. The author advises listening with healthy scepticism.

The author gives two reasons for scepticism. A leading firm in a fragmented industry may gain from scaring regulators into creating barriers to entry. Tech industry projections also have a long record of failing, and the note lists 19 examples.
earnings_insights: Mag7 earnings are flagged as heating up over the back half of the week, with no figures given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Five of six major domestic banks call for a 25bp hike and OIS prices over 80%. The Bloomberg median of 2.375% understates hike conviction.
Described as a 50-50 coin toss on its face. The author argues it is distorted by TD's double entries and non-specialist forecasters.
Better reflects the body of opinion than Bloomberg's consensus, though still diluted by non-specialists.
Focus pivots to the FOMC hold after US data on October 27.
Bullock testifies to parliament tonight, which may give a read on the next decision.
